Goal: Attendees find the app worth using rather than a chore
Metric: Average app star rating; count of ratings submitted
Hypothesis: 4.0+ suggests the app earned its place. Below 3.5 suggests it added friction. Very few ratings at all is itself a signal - people rate what they care about.

Goal: Attendees can tell speakers what landed
Metric: Average session star rating; count of ratings submitted
Hypothesis: Comments on more than a quarter suggests people felt heard. Ratings clustered on a few sessions suggests only strong reactions get recorded.

Goal: Attendees give speakers more than a star
Signal: Session rating carried a written comment
Metric: Ratings with has_comment=true / all session ratings
Hypothesis: A star is a reflex; a sentence is effort. Above 20% suggests people had something they wanted the speaker to hear.

Goal: Attendees can get in without help
Hypothesis: Below 85% means people are stuck at the code step - check spam placement and the 60s cooldown before blaming the code itself.

Goal: People install, because that is where notifications work
Signal: App launched from the Home Screen
Metric: Unique users firing home_screen_launch / unique signed-in users
Hypothesis: Low share explains weak notification reach: an uninstalled app cannot receive them on iOS.

Goal: Attendees opt in to being told what changed
Metric: Unique users granting permission / unique signed-in users
Hypothesis: Below half means schedule changes will not reach the room in time.

Metric: Unique users saving a profile / unique signed-in users
Hypothesis: Profiles arrive prefilled, so a low number is fine - it means we got the import right, not that people disengaged.

Goal: The feed is worth checking back on
Metric: Feed opens per user; count of attendee posts
Hypothesis: Posts from more than a handful of people suggests the feed reads as shared rather than a broadcast channel.

Goal: Attendees plan their day rather than drift through it
Metric: Unique users starring at least one session; stars per user
Hypothesis: Three or more stars per user suggests genuine planning rather than a curious tap.

Goal: Attendees discover what is on beyond the room they are in
Metric: Unique users viewing 2+ distinct tracks; breakdown by track
Hypothesis: If most people only ever see Main stage, the Demos and Open Sessions tracks are effectively invisible.

Goal: Attendees can find out what a session is about
Hypothesis: Programme opens with almost no session opens suggests the cards already answer the question - not necessarily a failure.

Tile name: Task success — Searches that found nobody
Goal: Attendees can find a specific person
Metric: % of searches returning zero results (lower is better; zero is the target)
Hypothesis: Zero-result searches above 20% suggests people search for something the directory does not hold - company, or topic.

Goal: The directory leads somewhere: a person's profile or their company
Hypothesis: Above 20% suggests the directory works as an introduction. Very low suggests people browse but never act.

Goal: A demo leads to the thing it demonstrated
Signal: Product link tapped on a demo session
Metric: Product link taps / demo session pages opened (session_page_opened where track = demos)
Hypothesis: This is the clearest commercial signal in the app: someone went looking for the product after the pitch.

Goal: Attendees reach the board where topics are proposed and voted on
Metric: Unique users tapping through; split before vs after the agenda lands
Hypothesis: Taps before the schedule is set are the ones that matter - they are the people who can still influence it.

Tile name: Retention — Return visits through the day
Goal: The app is used across the day, not opened once
Metric: People active in N or more separate hours of the event day (cumulative stickiness
Results: Three or more separate hours suggests it became the thing people check between talks.

Goal: Announcements are useful enough to act on, not noise
Metric: Unique users who opened a notification / unique users who enabled notifications
Hypothesis: Measured against people who enabled notifications, not against messages sent - the push service reports what it accepted, never what a phone chose to show, so a true delivered count does not exist to divide by.

Goal: See how far signed-in attendees got: set up, planned, and engaged with other people
Metric: Aha cohort / signed-in users; super user cohort / signed-in users. Aha = signed in AND saved a profile AND viewed all three room tabs AND opened a session AND starred one. Super = that AND viewed a profile AND opened the feed.
Hypothesis: Both are sets in any order, not sequences - so not a funnel. One tile, three bars: signed in at 100%, then each cohort as a share of it.
